hook: Seal some colorless N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> gas in a flask and watch: it turns brown, darker and darker, and then the color stops changing. Nothing seems to be happening any more. Yet if you could tag a single molecule, you would see it split apart and re-form again and again. The flask has reached chemical equilibrium, and the stillness hides constant motion.

prereq.q: In a reversible reaction, what is the reverse reaction?
options: Products reacting to re-form the reactants
The same reaction run at a lower temperature
Reactants forming a different set of products
prereq.why: A reversible reaction can run back: the products collide and react to give the original reactants.

prereq.q: A liquid in a sealed jar reaches a steady vapor pressure. What is true at that point?
options: Evaporation and condensation continue at equal rates
All of the liquid has evaporated
prereq.why: This is dynamic equilibrium: two opposite processes at equal rates, so nothing changes overall.

prereq.q: If the concentration of a reactant falls, what usually happens to the rate of the reaction that uses it?
prereq.why: Fewer reactant particles per liter means fewer collisions per second, so the rate drops.

figure.caption: In a sealed flask, the forward rate falls and the reverse rate rises until they are equal. From that moment the concentrations stop changing, but they are not equal.

chain.cause: Reactants are sealed in a closed container
chain.effect: only the forward reaction can run at first, at its fastest rate

chain.cause: Reactants are used up and products build up
chain.effect: the forward rate falls and the reverse rate rises
each species is made as fast as it is used, so every concentration stays constant

chain.cause: Both reactions keep running at equal rates
chain.effect: the equilibrium is dynamic: molecules still react, but the composition does not change

ideas: Chemical equilibrium: the forward and reverse rates are equal, so all concentrations are constant.
Constant does not mean equal. Equilibrium concentrations can be very different from each other.
Equilibrium is dynamic: both reactions continue. It is reached from either direction and only in a closed system.
On a concentration-time graph, equilibrium is where every curve becomes flat; changes before that follow the coefficients.

misconception.wrong: At equilibrium the reactions stop, and the reactants and products are present in equal amounts.
misconception.right: At equilibrium both reactions keep running at equal rates, so the amounts stay constant. The amounts are usually not equal; in the N₂O₄ flask, 0.0300 M N₂O₄ sits with 0.0400 M NO₂.

summary: In a closed container, a reversible reaction slows as reactants are used, while the reverse reaction speeds up as products build. When the two rates are equal, the system is at chemical equilibrium: every concentration is constant, but not equal, and both reactions keep running. Concentration changes follow the coefficients, and the same equilibrium is reached from either direction.
